title: afl-cassowire configuration
description:
Configuration file for afl-cassowire, the persistent-mode network proxy for afl-fuzz.

The loader (src/config.cpp) rejects unknown keys at every level except root keys starting with `__`, which are ignored and reserved for helper fragments: anchor reusable maps there (`__net: &net { ... }`) and reference them from real sections via aliases (`network: *net`) or merge keys (`<<: *net`). Nested sections do not allow `__`-prefixed keys. So additionalProperties is false throughout, with a patternProperties `^__` exemption at the root. YAML anchors and aliases work (e.g. `network_cmplog: *net`); merge keys (`<<`) are resolved by the loader. Scalar types are strict: ports/timeouts must be unquoted integers and booleans must be true/false. Note that JSON Schema cannot distinguish `!!binary` tagged scalars from plain strings, so payload prefix/suffix are modeled as strings.

target_cmplog.description: Compare-mode target, used instead of `target` when __AFL_CMPLOG_SHM_ID is set. Standalone: no key falls back to `target`. Ignored and not validated unless afl.enable_cmplog is true, in which case this section is required.

network_cmplog.description: Compare-mode network, used instead of `network` when __AFL_CMPLOG_SHM_ID is set. Standalone: no key falls back to `network` (the cmplog target may listen on a different port). To reuse the whole section unchanged: `network_cmplog: *net`. Ignored and not validated unless afl.enable_cmplog is true, in which case this section is required.

args.description: Full argv passed to execve; argv[0] goes first. When omitted, defaults to a single-element argv [binary]. When present it must be non-empty: an empty list is rejected by the loader.

env.description: Environment variables set for the target process (string -> string).

env_preserve.description: Parent environment inheritance: "nothing" (no vars), "afl_only" (PATH plus the AFL vars __AFL_SHM_ID, __AFL_CMPLOG_SHM_ID, ___AFL_EINS_ZWEI_POLIZEI___, AFL_DEBUG, AFL_DEBUG_CHILD, AFL_MAP_SIZE, AFL_NO_UI, AFL_QEMU_COMPCOV_DEBUG, AFL_QEMU_CMPLOG_DEBUG, AFL_QEMU_MAP_SIZE), or "all" (entire parent environment).

stdin_path.description: Optional path the proxy opens (read-only, non-blocking open with the flag cleared again afterwards) before fork and wires to the target's stdin (fd 0). Pure plumbing: the proxy never reads or writes it; it only satisfies targets that require a specific file on stdin - typically a fifo the surrounding setup creates and feeds. Must be non-empty; existence is checked at spawn time (an unopenable path aborts startup with a clear error). When absent, stdin stays /dev/null. The map-size pass always keeps /dev/null on stdin.

host.description: TCP host to connect to. Must be an IPv4 dotted-quad literal: the client uses inet_pton(AF_INET), and the loader rejects hostnames and IPv6 literals.

port.description: TCP port to connect to (required, 1-65535). Must match the port the target binds; port detection confirms this configured port.

probe.description: Post-response quiescence probe: after each response, open a throwaway connection and wait until the target services it (data/EOF/RST). Catches crashes in post-response cleanup within the same iteration. Disable for targets that rate-limit connections or cannot tolerate an extra short-lived connection.

probe_retry_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between probe retries when the first probe fails. Set to 0 for no delay (the loader default).

probe_attempts.description: Maximum number of quiescence-probe attempts per iteration (default 2). A failed probe never decides by itself: after each failure check_target_state() classifies the target - a dead target terminates the proxy immediately (SIGSEGV on crash, SIGABRT otherwise), a live target gets the next attempt after probe_retry_ms. Only when ALL attempts fail consecutively does the proxy abort so AFL respawns it.

enable_cmplog.description: Enable AFL compare log (requires __AFL_CMPLOG_SHM_ID). When true, the target_cmplog and network_cmplog sections become required.

cov_discard_init.description: Emit __AFL_COVERAGE_DISCARD() right before the first __AFL_LOOP pass so startup coverage (proxy init + target init in the shared map, plus the cmplog map) is not attributed to the first fuzzed testcase; the main stability knob. Requires the file-scope __AFL_COVERAGE() declaration. Setting this to false keeps the startup feedback from both the proxy and the target in the shared coverage map.

dump_history.description: Number of completed iterations whose payloads (prefix + input + suffix) are retained and written alongside a termination dump as <stem>.-1.data, <stem>.-2.data, ... (-1 = most recent previous iteration). A deferred/async crash is detected one iteration late, so the current payload may not be the input that caused it; the retained history preserves the likely culprit. 0 disables the history (only <stem>.data is written).

msg_log_level.description: Log level for the warn/error ring sink whose captured lines are embedded into termination .msg dumps. Affects dump content only; the console level is the --log-level CLI flag.

primary.description: Port detection method: "procfs" (scan /proc/net/tcp{,6}; polls waitpid(WNOHANG) every pass so a dying target is reported, and with verify_ownership: true the LISTEN entry must be owned by the target's process tree), or "seccomp" (the target runs with a SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF filter on bind()/listen() installed before its execve(); the proxy polls the notification fd, which aggregates those syscalls from every thread and forked descendant - kernel >= 5.0; readiness is confirmed with a bounded /proc scan, and subsequent socket poll() calls multiplex the notification fd alongside the data socket so later bind()/listen() notifications are answered immediately). Both methods work with QEMU-mode targets (threads and grandchild processes included); the old ptrace-based methods were removed.

verify_ownership.description: procfs only (silently ignored by seccomp, which verifies ownership by construction): the matched LISTEN entry in /proc/net/tcp{,6} must be attributable to the target - the socket inode (10th token of the line) must be held via a socket:[<inode>] readlink in /proc/<pid>/fd of the direct child or one of its descendants. A stale/foreign listener therefore fails detection after initial_ms instead of false-positiving; if the fd directory of a target-tree pid is unreadable (EACCES/EPERM, e.g. a setuid target that dropped privileges), the port is accepted unverified with a WARN. Independent of this flag, the procfs loop checks waitpid(WNOHANG) every pass, so a target that dies during startup reports TargetDied instead of a silent initial_ms stall.

enabled.description: Enable the pre-spawn port-conflict check/cleanup. Disabled by default: the proxy never scans /proc and a busy port surfaces through normal target/port-detection failure.

on_port_conflict.description: Behavior when cleanup.enabled and the configured port already has a LISTEN socket. "error": report the holder and refuse to start. "kill_orphan": SIGKILL only orphaned holders (no live parent: not a cmplog target, another campaign, or a service) of this exact port, provided the process matches the configured target binary/argv[0]; their process trees are killed too. There is no SIGTERM/grace phase. Live holders are never killed; the preflight refuses to start instead. Ignored when cleanup.enabled is false.

payload_section.description: Optional prefix/suffix wrapped around every payload sent to the target (in `proxy` and `test` mode): the transmitted data is prefix + fuzz input + suffix. Values may be plain strings or YAML `!!binary` base64-encoded bytes (a YAML tag, which JSON Schema cannot see - tagged scalars appear as plain strings here). Omit the section or a key to send the payload unmodified. A null section is accepted and treated as empty.

bytes_value.description: Raw bytes: plain string or YAML !!binary tagged scalar (base64-decoded by the loader).
